summary: Lower the implicit constructor of a base JavaScript class to a parameterless C# constructor when construction is statically parameterless and no class-constructor object semantics are observed.

target.notes: Emit a public parameterless constructor. JavaScript accepts extra arguments even when the default constructor declares none, so this rule requires all construction sites to be proven argument-free.

caveats: C# constructor overload resolution would reject extra arguments that JavaScript simply evaluates and ignores.

tests.name: implicit base constructor
tests.input: class C {} const c = new C(); console.log(c instanceof C);
tests.expected_csharp: public sealed class C { public C() { } }

tests.name: edge: extra arguments exclude native signature
tests.input: function sideEffect(){ console.log('arg'); return 1; } class C {} new C(sideEffect());
tests.expected_behavior: prints arg and construction succeeds; JavaScript evaluates and ignores the extra argument, so this rule must not match unless that behavior is separately lowered
